text:
House Buldbei’s rule, governed by the strongest claim, ended in ruin after twenty years. The power began with Lall Nealdgum holding the seat, but his standing collapsed as Pei Delve rose against it in 28. The house lost two places to the Galweall League—Pei Delve in 32 and Micrag in 42—and was finished in 42, its last follower scattering. Three people held the seat during this period: Lall Nealdgum, Hibrei Fou, and Thimseild Soldrind. Two were killed and one was cast out.

Lall Nealdgum’s rule ended when he was killed by Dreamwein Vous at Micrag in 34. Hibrei Fou took the seat that same year by the strongest claim. His rule was short; he was murdered by Thimseild Soldrind at Micrag in 39. Thimseild Soldrind, the named heir, took the seat after rejecting Bathwa Bea’s rival claim in 39. He was cast out in 42 for attempted murder. The seat passed from one person to another two times inside this period.

The Galweall League and House Buldbei fought three battles between them, all lost by Buldbei. The house sent out six raids: five were beaten off, and one carried off plunder from Themoor in 32. It suffered one raid on Micrag in 39, which got through but took nothing. Three people were cast out, and four exiles returned. The house’s standing had fallen to nothing before Pei Delve rose against it.

The period from 3 to 22 was defined by internal instability and a persistent, though ultimately unsuccessful, conflict with the Trostead Compact. House Buldbei began with Skengaer Tharsoull holding the seat, but his rule ended quickly when he was killed by Trurnur Draeltheas in year 7. The seat passed through four rulers in twenty years, with an average tenure of 3.8 years. The house faced four years of hunger at Pei Delve, which killed 41 people and drove 60 from their homes. Despite these internal crises, House Buldbei won both battles fought against the Trostead Compact at Pei Delve in years 9 and 10.

Violence and betrayal marked the succession of power. Trurnur Draeltheas took the seat by coup after killing Skengaer Tharsoull, but was himself murdered by Lall Nealdgum in year 9. Kesfound Thrael then took the seat by the strongest claim, only to be cast out by Lall Nealdgum in year 12. Two rulers were cast out and two were killed during this period. Threth Kruth, who had previously held the seat, was declared outlaw after his conspiracy against Kesfound Thrael was uncovered in year 10. The standing of the house fell to nothing in year 9, prompting Pei Delve to rise against it.

The conflict with the Trostead Compact began in year 9 when the Compact declared war on House Buldbei for Pei Delve. The Compact broke its alliance with House Buldbei that same year. House Buldbei and its allies defeated the Compact at Pei Delve in year 9, killing 23, and again in year 10, killing 18. Peace was made after two years of war. House Buldbei sent four raids during this period: one against Trostead in year 4 was beaten off; raids on Pellweagate in year 10 and Geirnpei Shafts in year 11 got through but took nothing; and a raid on Trostead in year 20 carried off 32 grain and killed 26. Lall Nealdgum held the seat at the end of the period.

The Galweall League’s decade was defined by internal collapse and violent succession. Its standing fell to nothing in 42, triggering a rebellion at Pei Delve, and it ended in 51 with Greimfourn Goul holding the seat after killing Mound Sith. The power began the period at war with House Buldbei, a conflict that lasted one year and ended with Buldbei’s destruction and the League taking Micrag. After that war, the League faced no external battles, but its internal stability vanished. Eight people held the seat in ten years, with the position passing seven times. Five rulers were killed, two were cast out, and one remained in power at the end.

Keandtei Taegro seized the seat in 42 through a coup against Lan Thraestun, who was cast out. Taegro’s rule lasted only a year before he was murdered by Del Monbirn at Trostead in 43. Veith Hei took the seat that same year by election, setting aside the claim of Haeldkeind Nen, who was cast out. Veith Hei’s tenure ended in 45 when Nond Mea challenged him openly and won. Nond Mea ruled for two years, surviving conspiracies by Del Monbirn and Vaswei Grand, both of whom were cast out. In 47, Rusund Gilteil challenged Nond Mea, won, and took the seat by coup, killing Nond Mea at Themoor.

Rusund Gilteil was murdered by Was Leithwon at Themoor in 48. Was Leithwon then took the seat by election, setting aside Peansith Rae, who was cast out. Was Leithwon’s rule was short; he was cast out in 49 after a conspiracy was uncovered. Varnnael Wansen took the seat by election in 48, but was murdered by Rend Greall at Themoor in 50. Mound Sith took the seat by election in 50. Greimfourn Goul challenged Mound Sith openly in 51, won, and killed him at Themoor, ending the period as the ruler. Throughout the decade, fifteen people were courted away from the ruler, reflecting a persistent pattern of defection.

The period of 43 marked the final collapse of House Buldbei, ending its rule through the mechanism of strongest succession. The house’s standing ended abruptly as it was defeated by the Galweall League, a power that operated by election.

In 43, the Galweall League and House Buldbei made peace, a diplomatic conclusion that followed the collapse of House Buldbei after one year of conflict. This peace settlement formalized the end of the house’s power.

The Trostead Compact’s nine-year existence ended in ruin, its power dismantled by a rival it had once bound through marriage. The period began with the Compact’s authority intact but fragile, marked by a failed raid on Geirnpei Shafts in 22 and a subsequent Galweall League raid on Trostead that killed 25 people but took nothing. The Compact’s internal stability proved as brittle as its external defenses. In 25, Tha Vu murdered Vun Doultheam, the ruler who had held the seat since 20, at Trostead. This act of internal violence triggered a succession crisis that the Compact could not resolve.

Besveir Maleal took the seat by right of birth in 25, but his rule was short-lived. Del Monbirn challenged him openly in 27, won, and took the seat, casting Besveir out. Tha Vu’s own conspiracy against Del Monbirn was uncovered after three years, leading to Tha Vu’s exile. The Compact attempted to secure its position through diplomacy, marrying Keandtei Taegro to Thimseild Soldrind in 28 to bind itself to the Galweall League. Yet this alliance did not prevent conflict. The Compact sent two raids, against Geirnpei Shafts in 22 and Gaehollow in 28, both of which were beaten off.

The Galweall League declared war on the Compact in 29 over a long-standing grievance, breaking its alliance with the Compact. The Galweall League and its allies defeated the Compact at Trostead, killing 167 people. The Galweall League took Trostead from the Compact, and the Compact was finished, its last 7 followers scattering. The period ended in 30 with peace between the Galweall League and the dissolved Compact. Three people held the seat during these years, each ruling for an average of 2.3 years. The Compact’s rule ended not by election or primogeniture, but by military defeat and dissolution.

The Trostead Compact spent twenty years defined by a fragile alliance with House Buldbei, a bond forged by three marriages in the first six years and broken by war in the ninth. The period began with the Compact occupying Geirnpei Shafts and ended with that same site lost to the Galweall League. Six people held the seat, passing five times, with three killed, one cast out, and one dying of natural causes. The Compact’s standing eroded through internal conspiracies, external defeats, and a famine that killed 209 people and displaced 214. It fought four battles, winning one and losing three, and sent four raids that all carried off plunder while suffering ten raids, four of which were beaten off.

At the start, Faellwil Na ruled the Compact until his death in year 4, after which Neinos Del took the seat by primogeniture, rejecting the claim of Frernli Peimeath. Neinos Del died in year 5, and Neallseis Staend succeeded him. Neallseis’s rule was challenged by Paepu Noth in a coup in year 10, which Paepu won, casting Neallseis out. Paepu Noth then ruled until his death in year 17, when Kesfound Thrael took the seat by right of birth. Kesfound Thrael was killed in year 20, and Vun Doultheam succeeded him, still holding the seat at the end of the period. The Compact’s relationship with House Buldbei shifted from alliance to enmity in year 9, when it declared war for Pei Delve and broke its alliance. House Buldbei and its allies defeated the Compact at Pei Delve in years 9 and 10, killing 23 and 18 respectively. The two sides made peace in year 11 after two years of war.

The Compact’s internal stability collapsed as its standing fell to nothing, prompting Pellweagate to rise in year 10 and Geirnpei Shafts to rise in year 15. Pellweagate later broke away as the Rising of Pellweagate in year 16, with Veith Hei taking its seat. A famine began at Geirnpei Shafts in year 6, killing 12 people and causing grain shortages that persisted for years, with further deaths in years 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 14, and 15. The Compact sent four raids against the Galweall League, targeting Gaehollow in years 3 and 16, and Themoor in years 4 and 18, all carrying off plunder. It suffered ten raids, including those by House Buldbei and the Galweall League, with Trostead raided in years 4, 5, 19, and 20. The Galweall League declared war on the Compact in year 19 over a long-standing grievance. The Compact defeated the Galweall League at Geirnpei Shafts in year 19, killing 19, but lost the site to them in year 20 after a battle where 16 died. The war ended in peace in year 21.

The Rising of Pellweagate spent its twenty-two years in a state of persistent failure, defined by external rejection and internal collapse. It began in year 16 when Veith Hei took the seat after Pellweagate broke from the Trostead Compact. The period was marked by a sequence of six raids, all of which were beaten off, and four years of hunger that killed 173 people. The power ended in year 36 when the Galweall League took Pellweagate and the Rising was finished, its last four followers scattering.

Veith Hei held the seat until year 32, a rule punctuated by famine and failed aggression. Hunger struck in years 19, 23, 27, and 30, killing 27, 55, 53, and 38 people respectively. During this time, the Rising sent out raids on Trostead in 19, Gaehollow in 31, Geirnpei Shafts in 32, Themoor in 33, Pei Delve in 34, and Trostead again in 35; every single one was beaten off. The internal stability of the rule eroded as exiles returned to service, including Beasre Feanwoul and Find Bound in year 26, and Besveir Maleal in year 33. Despite Find Bound marrying Draemo Grirn in year 27 to bind the Rising to the Trostead Compact, he challenged Veith Hei openly in year 32. Find Bound won, took the seat, and Veith Hei was cast out.

Find Bound’s rule lasted only four years before the Rising faced its end. In year 34, the Rising swore an alliance with House Buldbei, but this did not prevent its destruction. In year 36, the Galweall League declared war over a long-standing grievance, broke its alliance with the Rising, and defeated it at Pellweagate, where 136 people died. The Galweall League took Pellweagate from the Rising, and the Rising of Pellweagate was finished, landless, with its last four followers scattering. Peace was made between the Galweall League and the Rising in year 37, after the collapse of the Rising.

The Galweall League spent twenty years defined by a cycle of raids and retaliations against the Trostead Compact, a conflict that began with mutual violence and ended in exhaustion. At the start of the period, the League was bound to House Buldbei through the marriage of Paernso Feand and Trurnur Draeltheas. The Compact initiated hostilities by raiding Gaehollow in year 3 and Themoor in year 4, while the League responded with a raid on Trostead that was beaten off. Lald Neirntean, who held the seat, ordered the murder of Faellwil Na at Trostead in year 4, escalating the tension. The League’s military activity included five raids: three carried off plunder from Geirnpei Shafts and Pellweagate, one was beaten off, and one got through but took nothing.

Lald Neirntean consolidated power by absorbing exiles, including Gall Brolllea, Frernli Peimeath, Threth Kruth, Neallseis Staend, and Kesfound Thrael, who all returned to take service with the League. Despite this reinforcement, the League suffered further raids on Gaehollow and Themoor in years 16 and 18. In year 19, the League declared war on the Trostead Compact over a long-standing grievance, but was defeated at Geirnpei Shafts with 19 dead. The following year, the League and its allies defeated the Compact at the same site, killing 16, and took Geirnpei Shafts from them. During this time, Threth Kruth abandoned the League for the Compact, and Lald Neirntean ordered the murder of Kesfound Thrael.

The period ended with a shift in leadership and a cessation of hostilities. In year 21, Paernso Feand had Lald Neirntean murdered at Themoor, ending Lald’s rule. Threth Kruth took the seat by election, and the League made peace with the Trostead Compact after two years of war. Sealfeis Vearn married Beasre Feanwoul, binding the League to House Buldbei again. The League had fought two battles, one lost and one won, and held the seat through two rulers, one killed and one still holding at the end. The quarrel with the Trostead Compact remained the central feature, with two battles fought between them.

The Galweall League spent twenty years defined by violent succession and the destruction of its neighbors. It began under Threth Kruth, who held the seat since 21, and ended with Lan Thraestun taking the seat in 41. The period saw nine rulers, each holding power for an average of 2.1 years. The seat passed eight times, with four rulers cast out, three killed, one dying of natural causes, and one still holding at the end. The League fought four battles, winning all of them, and began three wars. It took three places: Trostead from the Trostead Compact in 29, Pei Delve from House Buldbei in 32, and Pellweagate from the Rising of Pellweagate in 36.

Threth Kruth ruled until his death in 30. During his reign, the League raided Trostead in 22, killing 25 but taking nothing. It declared war on the Trostead Compact in 29, breaking its alliance and defeating the Compact at Trostead, killing 167. The League took Trostead and the Compact finished. Threth died in Themoor in 30. Del Monbirn had Tha Vu murdered at Trostead that same year. Draemo Grirn took the seat in 30, setting aside the claim of Hibrei Fou, who was cast out. Thimseild Soldrind challenged Draemo in 31, lost, and was cast out. Besveir Maleal challenged and won in 32, taking the seat and casting out Draemo.

Besveir’s rule was short. Thimseild challenged him in 32, won, and took the seat by coup, casting out Besveir. The League declared war on House Buldbei in 32 over Pei Delve. It defeated House Buldbei at Pei Delve, killing 12, and took the site. Dreamwein Vous challenged Thimseild in 33, won, and took the seat, casting out Thimseild. Dreamwein had Lall Nealdgum murdered at Micrag in 34. Bathwa Bea attempted to kill Dreamwein in 35, failed, and was cast out and declared outlaw. Thaham Geth challenged Dreamwein in 36, won, and took the seat by coup, casting out Dreamwein. The League declared war on the Rising of Pellweagate in 36, defeated it at Pellweagate, killing 136, and took the site, finishing the Rising.

Thaham Geth ruled until 38. Laelldou Nerum challenged him in 38, won, and took the seat, killing Thaham at Themoor. Lurntu Skondbea challenged Laelldou in 39, won, and took the seat, killing Laelldou at Themoor. The League raided Micrag in 39, killing 29 but taking nothing. Find Bound challenged Lurntu in 40, lost, and was cast out. Lan Thraestun challenged Lurntu in 41, won, and took the seat, killing Lurntu at Themoor. Beasre Feanwoul attempted to kill Lan in 41, failed, and was cast out and declared outlaw. The League suffered 13 raids, all beaten off except one that carried off plunder. It sent two raids, both taking nothing. It fought House Buldbei in two battles, winning both.

In 51, Greimfourn Goul challenged Mound Sith openly for the Galweall League and won, taking the seat. Mound Sith was killed by Greimfourn Goul at Themoor.

The Galweall League spent 140 silver to buy back goodwill.

The Galweall League declared war on the Trostead Compact in 19, citing a long-standing grievance. The Trostead Compact defeated the Galweall League at Geirnpei Shafts in 19, where 19 people died.

In 20, Lald Neirntean had Kesfound Thrael murdered at Themoor. Later that year, the Galweall League and its allies defeated the Trostead Compact at Geirnpei Shafts, where 16 people died. The Galweall League took Geirnpei Shafts from the Trostead Compact.

The Galweall League and the Trostead Compact made peace in 21 after 2 years, both sides exhausted.

The Trostead Compact declared war on House Buldbei in year 9, seeking control of Pei Delve. House Buldbei and its allies defeated the Compact at that site in the same year, with 23 dead. The Compact suffered another defeat at Pei Delve in year 10, resulting in 18 dead.

The conflict lasted two years. In year 11, the Trostead Compact and House Buldbei made peace, both sides exhausted.
